subject: maths
question: One pipe can fill a tank in 6 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 9 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take total work = LCM(6, 9) = 18 units

Filling pipe = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 units/min, Emptying pipe = 18 ÷ 9 = 2 units/min

Net work = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/min

Half tank work = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 units ⇒ Time = 9 ÷ 1 = 9 min

**∴ Answer = 9 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling pipe = 6 min, Emptying pipe = 9 min

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 Person/Pipe
 Time (min)
 Total Work
 Efficiency
 
 
 
 

 Fill Pipe
 6
 18
 18 ÷ 6 = 3
 
 

 Empty Pipe
 9
 18 ÷ 9 = 2
 
 

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of (6, 9) = 18

⇒ Filling rate = 3 units/min, Emptying rate = 2 units/min

⇒ Net rate = 1 unit/min

⇒ Work for half tank = 9 units

⇒ Time = 9 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 9 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method

Assume total work as LCM of given times to simplify calculations and avoid fractions.

Net Efficiency

Net work = Filling rate − Emptying rate when pipes work together.

Work-Time Relation

Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

Half Work Concept

Time for half work = (Half work) ÷ Net efficiency
